name: Why Drainage Matters in Structural Repairs

mainEntity.name: How much does drainage affect foundation and retaining wall repairs?
mainEntity.text: How much does drainage affect foundation and retaining wall repairs?

acceptedAnswer.text: Drainage is often the hidden cause behind recurring structural damage. Water that collects near a foundation can weaken soil, increase pressure on walls, and create settlement or cracking over time. Retaining walls are especially vulnerable because trapped water adds force behind the wall. In Los Angeles County, sloped lots, irrigation runoff, and concentrated roof drainage can make the problem worse. A proper repair plan should identify where water is coming from, where it is going, and whether grading, drains, or downspout extensions are needed. If the contractor only talks about crack repair or wall patching, ask how they are addressing water movement. Solving drainage first is what helps the repair last.
acceptedAnswer.description: Drainage affects both foundation and retaining wall repairs because water pressure and soil saturation can cause movement, cracking, and settlement. If drainage is not corrected, the same damage often returns after the repair. A durable fix usually includes grading, downspout control, or drainage components, not just patching visible damage.
